citation_abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capability to generalize across diverse natural language processing tasks, inspiring the development of graph foundation models (GFMs) for large-scale pre-training. However, unlike language models with explicit token units, graphs lack a well-defined unit for generalization, making it challenging to design effective pre-training strategies. In this work, we propose REEF, a novel GFM framework that leverages relation tokens as the fundamental units. We construct a vocabulary of relation tokens to encode relational information within graphs. To accommodate diverse relations, we introduce two hypernetworks that adaptively generate the parameters of aggregators and classifiers in graph neural networks based on relation tokens. In addition, we design another hypernetwork to construct dataset-specific projectors and incorporate a dataset-level feature bias into the initial node representations, enhancing flexibility across different datasets with the same relation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that REEF consistently outperforms existing methods in both pre-training and transfer learning, highlighting its potential as a general-purpose graph foundation model.
